mappings.note: Which event '1857 की तोप' points to (the First War of Independence). Content comprehension of the poem's reference, so LO-4 -- not C-H2.1-LO-8, which is for responding to the poem's heritage/power message.
Meaning of the poem's phrase 'धर रखी गई है' (kept as a धरोहर). A gloss on the poet's wording, so LO-5; C-H2.1-LO-8 would be right only if a reaction to heritage conservation were asked.
Which war the cannon served in. Factual recall, LO-4 rather than LO-5.
When in the year the cannon is polished (Independence Day and Republic Day). A fact; the 'why twice a year' item is the heritage-reasoning one under C-H2.1-LO-8.
What the cannon tells the सैलानी about itself. Content of the poem's speaking-cannon passage, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
How the cannon is looked after (like the inherited Company Bagh). Recall of the poem's comparison, LO-4; the item that asks why heritage is looked after at all is C-H2.1-LO-8.
तात्पर्य of 'बहरहाल'. A शब्दार्थ gloss on the poem's colloquial diction, so LO-5 -- not C-H2.2, since no grammar operation is performed.
In what sense 'फ़ारिग' is used (free, vacant). Diction gloss, hence LO-5 rather than LO-4.
What the birds do sitting on the cannon (गपशप). This is the गौरैयों की गपशप प्रसंग that C-H2.1-LO-6 names; LO-4 would lose that the item is anchored on exactly that passage.
What the sparrows do in mischief (tamper with the cannon's parts). Squarely the गौरैया passage, so C-H2.1-LO-6 rather than C-H2.1-LO-7, which is about what their play symbolises.
Meaning of 'मुहाने' (entrance). Word gloss, so LO-5 and not LO-4.
What we have received as विरासत (the cannon). A factual recall, so LO-4; C-H2.1-LO-8 is for the items that ask the student to justify or respond to heritage conservation.
How the cannon's upkeep is done (polished twice a year). Fact, LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-8.
Whose सूरमा the cannon blew apart -- the freedom fighters of 1857. Content recall, so LO-4. (Its answer field holds a different question's answer plus a section banner; reported as a defect.)
Why inherited things are carefully preserved, to be explained at 3 marks. This is exactly the धरोहरों के संरक्षण strand of C-H2.1-LO-8; LO-4 would misread an argued response as factual recall.
What the poem tells us about the cannon. The answer is the assembled facts of the poem, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-8.
What सीख the cannon in the Company Bagh gives -- that power must fall silent, and that the martyrs are to be remembered. That is the poem's संदेश on सत्ता के अंत, so C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than LO-4.
Which two occasions the twice-yearly polishing refers to (15 August, 26 January). A factual inference from the poem, so LO-4 and not C-H2.1-LO-8.

Sets the 'छोटे लड़कों की घुड़सवारी ... चिड़िया ही अकसर करती हैं गपशप' stanza for explication -- the गपशप प्रसंग itself, with its irony that a terror of 1857 is now a plaything. C-H2.1-LO-6, not LO-5, because the outcome names this passage.

Sets 'कितनी भी बड़ी हो तोप एक दिन तो होना ही है उसका मुँह बंद' for explication -- what the birds on the dead cannon stand for. C-H2.1-LO-7 rather than LO-6, since the deliverable is the symbol, not the gossip scene.
Sets 'उड़ा दिए थे मैंने अच्छे-अच्छे सूरमाओं के धज्जे' for explication. This is the cannon's own boast about the past, not the birds' passage, so LO-5 rather than C-H2.1-LO-6 or LO-7.
What the poet means by 'अच्छे-अच्छे सूरमाओं के धज्जे'. Construing that phrase and its bitterness is भाव-पक्ष, so LO-5; neither bird-specific outcome applies.
What information the poem gives about the cannon, enumerated. Content, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-8.
'भाव स्पष्ट करें' on the same 'मुँह बंद' lines -- the lifeless cannon as the emblem of power's end. C-H2.1-LO-7, not LO-5, because the outcome exists precisely for this analysis.
What संदेश the cannon gives -- never misuse power, fear no aggressor. The poem's message on सत्ता के अंत, so C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than LO-4.
Why the 1857 cannon is polished twice a year, at 5 marks -- the answer argues its historical and heritage value. C-H2.1-LO-8, unlike the 1-mark items that merely ask when, which are LO-4.
'Prove, from the poem, that inherited things are carefully preserved.' A reasoned response on धरोहरों का संरक्षण, hence C-H2.1-LO-8 and not LO-4.

Same heritage-preservation prompt, mapped C-H2.1-LO-8 for the same reason. Its stem has swallowed the model answer and its answer field holds an unrelated option '(घ) अनुप्रास' -- reported as a defect, not mapped around.
When the सैलानी come to the Company Bagh (morning and evening). Factual recall, LO-4 rather than LO-5.

Why the cannon is set at the Bagh's mouth -- so visitors remember the martyrs of 1857. That memorial purpose is the heritage strand of C-H2.1-LO-8; the sibling item whose answer is merely 'so people can see it easily' is LO-4.
Meaning of 'जबर' (= शक्तिशाली). A gloss on the poem's colloquial word, so LO-5 and not C-H2.2.
On what the birds sit and gossip (the cannon). The गपशप प्रसंग again, so C-H2.1-LO-6 rather than plain LO-4.
What the cannon is used for now (boys' horse-riding). The children's play, not the birds', so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-6 or LO-7.
What the boys do on the cannon (ride it). Content recall about the children, so LO-4 and not the bird-specific outcomes.
Which war the cannon served in -- a repeat of the earlier recall item, mapped LO-4 the same way.
Meaning of 'विरासत' (what forebears leave behind). A शब्दार्थ gloss, so LO-5; C-H2.1-LO-8 covers responding to the heritage message, not defining the word.
Which two inherited things the poem describes (कंपनी बाग and तोप). Factual recall, LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-8.
Why the British built Company gardens (for their own use). A contextual fact behind the poem, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
Grasp the poem's भाव and render it in prose. The deliverable is the whole poem's sense recast -- भाव-पक्ष व्याख्या, so LO-5 rather than any single-passage outcome.
What the sparrows and birds tell us -- that one day even the biggest cannon's mouth is shut. The symbolic reading of the birds on the dead cannon, so C-H2.1-LO-7 rather than LO-6's gossip scene.
Whose sufferings the cannon recounts (Indians'). Factual recall, so LO-4 and not C-H2.1-LO-8.
What सीख the cannon gives (not to repeat past mistakes, not to trust a foreign power again). A response to the poem's message, hence C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than LO-4.
Whose upkeep the poem describes (the cannon's). Plain recall, LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-8.
What the cannon serves as now (a toy and a monument). Content recall, so LO-4; the item asking what that reversal symbolises is C-H2.1-LO-7.
Who gets inside the cannon (the birds). Part of the गौरैयों की गपशप/शैतानी passage, so C-H2.1-LO-6 rather than plain LO-4.
The hallmark of Viren Dangwal's poetry (depicting the ordinary people). कवि-परिचय, which none of the poem-bound outcomes covers, so the literature competency.
Which poem the line 'एक दिन तो होता ही है उसका मुँह बंद' is from. Text identification across a set of poems, so C-H2.3 rather than C-H2.1-LO-7, which asks what the line means.
Who wrote 'तोप'. Authorship identification, hence C-H2.3 and not a poem-comprehension outcome.
Why the cannon stands at the entrance -- so that no East India Company can come again. That warning is the poem's message on power, so C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than LO-4.
Who used this cannon (the British, in 1857). Factual recall, so LO-4 and not C-H2.1-LO-8.
Why the cannon is at the मुहाना -- here answered practically, so that passers-by can see it. Content, LO-4; the sibling item whose answer is the memorial purpose is C-H2.1-LO-8.
What the cannon says about itself (that it was once very powerful). Content of the speaking-cannon passage, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.

Which collection won the prize ('इसी दुनिया'). A literary-award fact of the poet's career, so C-H2.3. Note the stem names श्रीकांत वर्मा while the answer is Viren Dangwal's collection -- reported as a defect.
What संदेश the poet gives through the cannon (do not repeat the past's mistakes). The poem's message, hence C-H2.1-LO-8 and not LO-4.
What message the birds give -- every powerful man's mouth is shut one day like the cannon's. The symbolic reading of the birds on the cannon, so C-H2.1-LO-7 rather than LO-6.
Who comes to the Company Bagh morning and evening (सैलानी). Factual recall, LO-4 and not LO-5.
What सीख the cannon gives -- a repeat of the earlier सीख item, mapped C-H2.1-LO-8 for the same reason rather than LO-4.

How, per the poet, problems should be solved (by talking, not by guns). A reader's response to the poem's stance on force and power, so C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than LO-4. Its options (क) and (घ) are identical -- reported.
Why the British army used the cannon (to crush Indian patriots). A historical fact behind the poem, so LO-4 and not C-H2.1-LO-8.
What the cannon reminds us of (the freedom struggle). Content recall; the items asking what सीख or संदेश follows from that are the C-H2.1-LO-8 ones.
